turns.tutor:
Happy to. Since adding -s after he, she and it is mostly secure, let's sharpen the spelling side and one tricky case.
A quick reminder: most verbs just add -s (plays, drinks, lives). Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -s, -x or -o add -es (watches, goes). A consonant plus y becomes -ies (cries), but a vowel plus y keeps the y (plays).
Example of my own: My neighbour finishes work at six, goes to the gym, and then relaxes at home.
Your task: write two sentences about someone's weekly routine. Use at least three different verbs, with one -es verb and one consonant + y verb. Then say which rule each verb follows.
